record.context_brief: whether self-inverting series are automatically Hessian nilpotent
record.original_question: Suppose P(z) is a formal power series in C[[z]] with order at least 2 and with (Hes P)(0) nilpotent, so that its inversion pair Q(z) is defined by the symmetric formal map F(z) = z - grad P(z) and its formal inverse G(z) = z + grad Q(z). If P is self-inverting, meaning that its inversion pair satisfies Q(z) = P(z), must every self-inverting polynomial or formal power series automatically be Hessian nilpotent?

evidence.quote: Definition 4.1. A formal power series P(z) in C[[z]] with o(P(z)) >= 2 and (Hes P)(0) nilpotent is said to be self-inverting if its inversion pair Q(z) = P(z).
Open Problem 4.8. (a) Decide whether or not all self-inverting polynomials or formal power series are HN.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Work in the ring $\mathbb{C}[[z]] = \mathbb{C}[[z_1,\dots,z_n]]$ of formal power series in $n$ variables. For $P(z) \in \mathbb{C}[[z]]$, let $\nabla P = (\partial P/\partial z_1,\dots,\partial P/\partial z_n)$ denote its gradient and $\operatorname{Hes} P = (\partial^2 P/\partial z_i\partial z_j)$ its Hessian matrix. Write $o(P)$ for the order of $P$ (the lowest total degree of a nonzero monomial). 

Assume $o(P) \geq 2$ and that $(\operatorname{Hes} P)(0)$ is a nilpotent matrix. Define the formal symmetric map 
$$F(z) = z - \nabla P(z).$$ 
Under these hypotheses $F$ has a formal inverse $G(z)$, which can be written uniquely in the form 
$$G(z) = z + \nabla Q(z)$$ 
for some $Q(z) \in \mathbb{C}[[z]]$ with $o(Q) \geq 2$. The series $Q$ is called the inversion pair of $P$.

The series $P$ is called Hessian nilpotent (HN) if $\operatorname{Hes} P$ is nilpotent as a matrix over $\mathbb{C}[[z]]$ (not merely at $0$). The series $P$ is called self-inverting if its inversion pair satisfies $Q(z) = P(z)$.

Question: Must every self-inverting formal power series (or polynomial) $P(z) \in \mathbb{C}[[z]]$ be Hessian nilpotent?
artifact.status_search_result: The question was posed as an open problem in the literature on Hessian nilpotent polynomials and their connection with the Jacobian conjecture (via the vanishing conjecture). Available search results discuss this circle of problems but do not indicate a published resolution of whether every self-inverting formal power series is automatically Hessian nilpotent. Status could not be definitively verified.

status_evidence.title: Some properties of and open problems on Hessian nilpotent polynomials
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses properties and open problems on HN polynomials and their (deformed) inversion pairs.
status_evidence.claim: The problem belongs to a list of open problems on Hessian nilpotent polynomials and inversion pairs.

status_evidence.title: Hessian Nilpotent Polynomials and the Jacobian Conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: Reduces the Jacobian conjecture to a vanishing conjecture about Hessian nilpotent polynomials.
status_evidence.claim: Hessian nilpotent polynomials and their inversion pairs are central to research on the Jacobian conjecture; no resolution of the self-inverting question is reported.

status_evidence.title: Two results on homogeneous Hessian nilpotent polynomials
status_evidence.snippet: Proves results on homogeneous HN polynomials.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work addresses related HN polynomial questions but does not announce a resolution to the self-inverting/HN question.
